instruction.literal:
Take the FIRST entry of the `packages` list bound below and
work only that package. `pr` names the repository, the pull
request number and the head sha to work against.

A package is one rule in one file, and every finding id in it
is answered by ONE change — thirteen instances of a literal
duplication are one constant, not thirteen commits. Do not
re-rank the packages, do not merge two of them, and do not
touch findings outside the one you took: the analysis already
decided that the rest of this file waits for the re-scan after
your push, when their line numbers are current again.

Implement the fix on a branch and open or update a pull request
for it. NEVER merge anything: this graph's merge step is a
separate human-approval node, and an agent merging here would
bypass it.

If the package is not actually a defect — a false positive, or
one whose fix would be wrong — say so plainly and submit
`no_change` with the reason. A stated non-fix is a better
outcome than a manufactured one.

Report which package you took, what you changed, and the PR you
opened or updated.
